terms.comment: Plural frāga, frāgōrum n. pl., strawberries. Ancient frāgum referred to strawberries known to the ancients. Applying it to today’s cultivated garden strawberry is ordinary modern usage, not a claim that the modern hybrid existed in antiquity.

phrases.latin: Frāga lavā et in catīnum pōne.
phrases.english: Wash the strawberries and put them in the bowl.

phrases.latin: Ecce frāga silvestria! Lege quot vīs.
phrases.english: Look, wild strawberries! Pick as many as you like.

phrases.latin: Quī legitis flōrēs et humī nāscentia frāga, frīgidus, ō puerī, fugite hinc, latet anguis in herbā.
phrases.english: You who pick flowers and strawberries growing low on the ground, run away from here, children: a cold snake is lurking in the grass.
they gathered the fruit of the strawberry tree and mountain strawberries

sources: Lewis & Short: fragum · Lewis & Short: silvestris
John C. Traupman, Conversational Latin for Oral Proficiency, p. 73.
